subject: Riverfront AI — pilot SLOs, model fit, and topology next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@riverfront.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T15:24:00Z
Subject: Riverfront AI — pilot SLOs, model fit, and topology next steps

Alex — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps from Redwood's side.

Highlights / pain we heard
- Tail latency spikes are driving cancellations on peak pages (observed spikes up to 800ms on 95th+ during heavy traffic).
- Cost per active conversation is a gating factor for expansion — currently over target when using the larger model.
- Data residency & compliance: EU customer traffic must stay in eu-west region; procurement will want an SLA and a simple MAP.

Goals you stated
- Maintain response quality for multi-turn chat (avg response ~400 tokens).
- Target tail latency goals: p95 < 250ms for 512-token prompts, p50 < 70ms.
- Sustained throughput target: ~150–200 req/s with short spikes to 300 rps for bursts.
- Observable metrics and clear rollback/fallback behavior for degraded conditions.

Initial technical notes (from our side)
- Model candidates: Llama2-13B (quantized int8/int4) as the primary candidate for pilot QPS; Llama2-70B reserved for a quality-focused canary if latency is acceptable with Dedicated capacity.
- KV/prefix caching: will likely cut effective latency for repeated prompts — propose a 30m TTL for warm-up during the pilot.
- Batching: aim for a 20–40ms batching window with dynamic batch thresholds per tenant to meet p50 targets while keeping p95 under control.
- Topology options discussed: Dedicated Redwood pool (preferred) in eu-west for residency, multi-region read fallback to us-east for non-EU traffic, and routing policy based on region + priority tier.

Attachments I attached here: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (MAP draft), redwood_sla_draft.docx (SLA + uptime targets), topology-profile-diagram.png (initial topology sketch).

Proposed next steps and owners
- Redwood to run three microbenchmarks (13B int8, 13B int4, 70B int8) against sample prompts you provide — due Oct 8. (Owner: Jordan)
- Delivery of MAP + SLA draft for your procurement by Oct 6. (Owner: Karthik)
- Technical deep-dive call with Redwood infra + Riverfront infra to validate network/topology on Oct 9 — please confirm availability. (Owner: Irene to coordinate)
- You to share: representative prompt set, 1-hour peak tps profile, and any compliance checklist items (data retention windows).

If that aligns, I’ll queue the benchmark work and share the MAP + SLA draft by next Tuesday.

— Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@riverfront.ai>

Date: 2026-10-02T18:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Riverfront AI — pilot SLOs, model fit, and topology next steps

Karthik — thanks for the write-up, that’s helpful and mostly aligns. A couple clarifications before you start benchmarks:

- Our average response length is ~350–450 tokens, with a long-tail of up to ~900 tokens on certain support flows. Please include a 512-token and 800-token scenario in the tests.
- For compliance: EU traffic must not egress to us-based logging buckets. Access logs are fine if kept in eu-west; redact PII before any external transfer.
- Regarding throughput: our initial pilot target is 150 sustained rps, but real-world can spike to ~320 rps for 2–3 minutes. If you can show graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model or queued responses) that’s ideal.

We can confirm Oct 9 for the deep dive — both Maya and I are available in the morning (09:00–11:30 CET).

I’ll upload the sample prompts and a 60-minute peak trace to the Drive folder you shared by EOD tomorrow.

— Alex
CTO, Riverfront AI
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Soto <alex.soto@riverfront.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Riverfront AI — pilot SLOs, model fit, and topology next steps

Looping in a few infra/solutions notes from my end after the call:

Quick recommendations
- Run Dedicated pool in eu-west with Reserved capacity (N GPUs) for the 70B canary. For the 13B pilot we can use a mix of Dedicated low-priority nodes + burstable hosted capacity to optimize cost.
- Model quantization: start with int8 for correctness checks, then test int4 for 13B to drop memory and improve QPS — validate quality delta on your key prompts.
- Sharding & kernels: 70B will need tensor + pipeline parallelism; suggest testing on 4xA100-80GB equivalence for initial latency numbers.
- KV cache strategy: pre-warm most frequent prefixes (top 5% of queries) and keep a 30m TTL; implement cold-miss fast fallback to smaller model to avoid long tails.
- Batcher policy: dynamic batch timeouts — 15ms aggressive for low-latency route, up to 40ms when throughput optimization is preferred.

Benchmarks we'd deliver
- Latency/throughput matrix for the three configurations (13B int8, 13B int4, 70B int8) at payload sizes 256/512/800 tokens.
- 99/95/50 latency percentiles, and memory/CPU utilization per GPU.
- A simulated burst test (320 rps for 3 minutes) showing routing/fallback behavior.

Data & access asks from Riverfront
- Representative prompt set (as Alex noted).
- Peak-hour traffic trace (anonymized).
- Any IP allowlist info if you want to test network egress constraints from your side.

I’ll attach an updated topology sketch (topology-profile-diagram.png) with the Dedicated pool + regional fallback lanes. Jordan — can you pick up the benchmark run once we have the prompts?

— Irene
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference

Alex — quick confirmation after internal sync:

Committed deliverables & dates
- MAP (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) + SLA draft (redwood_sla_draft.docx): delivered Oct 6. (Owner: Karthik)
- Benchmark runs (13B int8, 13B int4, 70B int8) using your prompts: start Oct 5, deliver results Oct 8. Includes latency matrix (p50/p95/p99), throughput ceilings, and a 3-minute burst sim. (Owner: Jordan)
- Tech deep-dive: Oct 9 at 09:30 CET — agenda to include network topology review, test plan walkthrough, and fallback policy. (Owner: Irene to send calendar invite)
- Follow-up: if benchmarks show the 70B option meets p95 <= 250ms for 512 tokens, we’ll scope a limited canary (10% traffic) in eu-west. If not, we’ll recommend the 13B int4 path and iterate on caching/batching rules.

Help from Riverfront: please share the prompt set + 60-min peak trace and confirm whether we can run a controlled load test against a staging endpoint with IP allowlist by Oct 5.

Thanks — we’ll get the drafts into the Drive and a calendar invite for Oct 9 out today.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
